title: AI art around a Z-machine; Zork's thief makes pre-rendering tricky
author: transfire
selftext:
I've been building Overlore on top of a Z-machine interpreter I wrote in Crystal. It runs the original game's rules and text. AI paints rooms, voices narration, and provides a dungeon master, but the engine stays in charge of state.

For visual continuity, a player's first portrait becomes a reference for later scenes. The first image of a room also uses neighboring rooms as references. I index finished assets by properties and semantic similarity so later players can reuse them instead of generating everything again.

To keep things snappy, I start painting likely next rooms while the current narration plays. Then Zork's thief wanders into or out of one of those rooms, and the image I started may no longer fit the state the player reaches. I wrote up that problem, the imperfect character consistency, and an early miss with a white house whose windows weren't boarded when the game later said they were. You can read about it here:

[https://trans.github.io/blog/posts/2026-10-28-the-other-half-of-the-holodeck.html](https://trans.github.io/blog/posts/2026-10-28-the-other-half-of-the-holodeck.html)

The game isn't publicly playable yet, but you can meet a Bard and see ten real game screenshots at the game's future website [https://overlore.xyz](https://overlore.xyz)

Hmm... maybe the thief has a movement pattern I can use. Think I'll go check into that...

comments.author: deeplifeaspirant
comments.body: Separating the thief into an overlay might let you reuse the room image when he moves. Matching the lighting would be tricky, though.

replies.author: transfire
replies.body:
Thanks! And yes the lighting is the exact issue I ran into. 

I did find a \*half\* solution though. I can generate an image with the thief and then generate another, specifically asking for the same exact image with the thief removed, and then diff the two images to extract the thief. I works pretty well. This doesn't allow me to reuse the thief's image anywhere but it does allow me to use in that room with other objects I extract the same way... well mostly, sometimes a cast shadow in the scene can frump it up. So I am not quite out of the woods on that approach yet either.
